more_info.banned_in:
Approved in the EU.
Approved in the US.
US food use is subject to the listed CFR provisions and their conditions, checked in 2026.
No current country-wide food-use ban was confirmed in the regulatory sources checked in 2026.
The permissions checked in 2026 apply only to the specified preparations, food uses and conditions.
more_info.overview: Aspartame is the methyl ester of an aspartic-acid and phenylalanine dipeptide, approximately 200 times as sweet as sucrose. It provides sweetness when added to the food or used in a table-top sweetener preparation. The specified material is supplied as white powder or crystalline material. Only a limited amount dissolves in water, according to the specification.
more_info.uses:
Examples in the EU food-use list include certain cocoa and Chocolate products as covered by Directive 2000/36/EC; other confectionery including breath freshening microsweets; chewing gum; decorations, coatings and fillings, except fruit-based fillings covered by category 4.2.4; fruit nectars as defined by Directive 2001/112/EC and vegetable nectars and similar products; flavoured fermented milk products including heat-treated products.
The entries apply to particular food categories and may limit the amount, the preparation or the way it is used; they do not show how often the additive appears in retail products.
more_info.side_effects:
Reported food-use estimates were below the limit in the 2026 assessment.
The reviewed evidence did not identify a new genotoxicity concern or a better dose for deriving the limit.
more_info.precautions: US labels must identify phenylalanine for people with phenylketonuria, because aspartame supplies phenylalanine.
